la:noun:sitis.html:
sĭtis, is (abl. site, Ven. Carm. 2, 13, 3; acc. sitem, Prud. στεφ. 2, 250), f.
etym. dub.; perh. akin with siccus
,
thirst (class.; used only in sing.).
Lit.: demum fodere puteum, ubi sitis fauces tenet,; cf.: tibi cum fauces urit sitis,: siti sicca sum,: anum interfecero siti fameque atque algu,; ; cf.: cum cibo et potione fames sitisque depulsa est,: explere diuturnam sitim,; cf.: ut sitim nostro possis explere cruore,: ubi quarta sitim caeli collegerit hora,excited,: fessa labore sitim collegerat,had become thirsty,: sitim tolerare,: exstinguere sitim,: restinguere,: pellere,; : finire,: sedare,; ; ; : famem ac sitim sedare,; : levare,; : relevare, al.: compescere,: deponere,: defendere fonte,: avertere,: reprimere,: pomi sitim faciunt,provoke,: sucus, qui sitim stimulet,: sitim adferunt (fici),: accendit,; : in lassitudine et in siti,: excessit sitim potio,was more than enough for,: ardere siti,: sitis arida guttur Urit,.—
Transf., of things (places, plants, etc.), dryness, drought, aridity (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): et Canis arenti torreat arva siti,; : deserta siti regio,: haurit sitis ignea campos,: sitis aestatis restinguitur fontibus, i. e. of plants,; —
Trop., strong or ardent desire, greediness, thirst: cupiditatis sitis,.—With gen. obj.: libertatis,: cruoris,: argenti sitis importuna famesque,: sitis major famae quam virtutis,: audiendi,.

senses: to thirst for, long for, desire eagerly
la:verb:sitio.html:
sĭtĭo, īvi or ĭi, 4, v. n. and a.
[sitis].
Neutr., to thirst, be thirsty (class.).
Lit.: ego esurio et sitio,; : sitit haec anus,: in medio sitit flumine potans,: ne homines sitirent,.—With gen.: cochleae cum sitiunt aëris,.—Prov.: sitire mediis in undis,i. e. to be poor in the midst of wealth,.—
Transf. (esp. in the lang. of country people), of things (the earth, plants, etc.), to be dried up or parched, to want moisture: siquidem est eorum (rusticorum) gemmare vites, sitire agros, laetas esse segetes, etc.,; cf.: sitire segetes,: tosta sitit tellus, Ov.

F. 4, 940: colles,; cf. infra, P. a.: aret ager; vitio moriens sitit aëris herba,: cum sitiunt herbae,: arbores,: cacumina oleae, et saep.: ipsi fontes jam sitiunt,: nec pati sitire salgama,to be dry,.—

Act., to thirst after a thing (rare, but in the trop. signif. class.; cf.: cupio, desidero).
Lit.: auriferum Tagum sitiam patriumque Salonem,.—Pass.: quo plus sunt potae, plus sitiuntur aquae,are thirsted for,: umor quomodo sititur destillans,.—
Trop., as in all langg., to long for, thirst for, desire eagerly, covet: sanguinem nostrum sitiebat,; cf. : sanguinem, (opp. satiare); : cruorem, Poët. ap. ; cf.: sitit hasta cruores,: honores,: populus libertatem sitiens,: ultionem, ext. 6; .—With gen.: non quidem fallacis undae sitit, sed verae beatitudinis esurit et sitit,.—Hence, sĭtĭens, entis, P. a., thirsting, thirsty, athirst.
Lit.: ut ipse ad portam sitiens pervenerim,: quae (pocula) arenti sitientes hausimus ore,: Tantalus,: viator,: saecla ferarum,: sitienti aqua datur,.—
Transf. (acc. to I. B.), of places, plants, etc., dry, parched, arid, without moisture (syn. aridus): hortus,.—By metonymy also, Afri, : olea,: luna,i. e. cloudless, bright,; : Canicula,arid, parching,.—Neutr. plur. absol.: lonchitis nascitur in sitientibus,in dry, arid places,; so, in sitientibus aut siccis asperis,.—With gen.: sitientia Africae,.—
Trop., thirsting for, desiring eagerly, greedy: gravius ardentiusque sitiens,: (amator) avidus sitiensque,: regna Ditis, Petr. poët. 121, 116: aures,.—Poet.: modice sitiens lagena,of moderate capacity,.—With gen.: virtutis,: famae,: pecuniae (with avarus et avidus),: sermonis,.—Hence, adv.: sĭtĭenter, thirstily, eagerly, greedily (acc. to B.): sitienter quid expetens,; so, incumbere hauriendis voluptatibus,: haurire salutares illas aquas,; , p. 135, 35.

la:noun:situs.gloss: decay, rust, mould, mustiness, dust, dirt; soil
senses: decay, rust, mould, mustiness, dust, dirt; soil
a rusting, moulding or wasting away, dullness, inactivity
la:noun:situs.html:
sĭtus, ūs, m.
sino
.
(Sino, 1. situs, A.; prop. a being laid or placed, a lying; hence, by meton.)
The manner of lying, the situation, local position, site of a thing (class. in sing. and plur.; mostly of localities; syn. positus).
Sing.: terrae,: urbem Syracusas elegerat, cujus hic situs esse dicitur,: loci,: urbis,; ; ; : locorum,; : Messana, quae situ moenibus portuque ornata est,; cf.: urbes naturali situ inexpugnabiles,; : agri (with forma),: Africae,: castrorum,; : montis,: loca naturae situ invia,; opp. opus: turrem et situ et opere multum editum,; ; cf. : figura situsque membrorum,; cf.: passeres a rhombis situ tantum corporum differunt,: Aquilonis,towards the north,.—Poet.: exegi monumentum aere perennius Regalique situ pyramidum altius, i. e. the structure (prop. the manner of construction), (cf. the Part. situs, in Tac., = conditus, built; v. sino, P. a. A. 2. c.).—
Plur.: opportunissimi situs urbibus,; so, oppidorum,: terrarum,; cf. : locorum,: castrorum,: situs partium corporis, : revocare situs (foliorum),position, arrangement,. —
Transf. (= regio), a quarter of the world, region (Plinian): a meridiano situ ad septentriones,; ; ; cf. Sill. ad .—Plur.: (pantherae) repleturae illos situs,.—
Soil (late Lat.): quae loca pingui situ et cultu,.—
Description (late Lat.): cujus originem in Africae situ digessimus plene,.—
Lit.
Rust, mould, mustiness, dust, dirt, etc., that a thing acquires from lying too long in one place (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; not in Cic. or Cæs.; syn.: squalor, sordes): corrumpor situ,; cf.: quae in usu sunt et manum cottidie tactumque patiuntur, numquam periculum situs adeunt,: tristia duri Militis in tenebris occupat arma situs,: arma squalere situ ac rubigine,: immundo pallida mitra situ,ne aut supellex vestisve condita situ dilabatur,: per loca senta situ,: araneosus situs,: immundus,; cf. ; : detergere situm ferro,: deterso situ,: prata situ vetustatis obducta,. —
Filthiness of the body: genas situ liventes, Poët. ap. (Com. Rel. p. 225 Rib.: situm inter oris et barba, etc.): en ego victa situ,; ; ; ; ; .—
Trop.
Neglect, idleness, absence of use: indigna est pigro forma perire situ,: et segnem patiere situ durescere campum,; : gladius usu splendescit, situ rubiginat,. —
Of the mind, a rusting, moulding, a wasting away, dulness, inactivity: senectus victa situ,: marcescere otio situque civitatem,: situ obsitae justitia, aequitas,: quae (mens) in hujusmodi secretis languescit et quendam velut in opaco situm ducit,; cf. : ne pereant turpi pectora nostra situ,: depellere situm curis,: flebis in aeterno surda jacere situ (carmina),i. e. oblivion,: (verba) priscis memorata Catonibus Nunc situs informis premit et deserta vetustas,; cf.: verborum situs,: nec umquam passure situm,: passus est leges istas situ atque senio emori,.

la:noun:situlus.gloss: a vessel used to hold water

la:noun:sitella.html:
sĭtella, ae, f.dim.
situla
,
a kind of urn used in drawing lots. It was made narrow at the top, so that but one lot at a time could be on the surface of the water with which it was partly filled, ; ; ; 2, 6, 11; 2, 6, 44: sitellam detulit,: de M. Octavio deferre sitellam,: sitella lata est, ut sortirentur, Weissenb. ad loc.; 41, 18, 8.

la:noun:situla.gloss: a vessel used to hold water
senses: a vessel used to hold water
a voting urn (for drawing lots or holding voting tablets); loosely, a ballot box
la:noun:situla.html:
sĭtŭla, ae, f. (
masc. collat. form sĭtŭ-lus, ; ; ; Fest. s. v. nanum, pp. 176 and 177 Müll.; ).
A bucket for drawing water, ; ; Poët. ap. Anthol. Burm. 1, p. 493; Non. s. v. creterra, p. 375, 6 Gerl.; cf. Becker, Gallus, 2, p. 268 (2d edit.).—
An urn, used in drawing lots (instead of the usual sitella), .
